value.zh: 行本，璠兄子也。
value.en: Xingben was the son of Fan's elder brother.
value.literal: Xingben was Fan's elder brother's son.

value.zh: 父環，仕梁，曆職清顯。
value.en: His father Huan served Liang and successively held clear, eminent posts.
value.literal: His father Huan served Liang and successively held clear, eminent posts.

value.zh: 行本起家梁武陵王國常侍。
value.en: Xingben first entered office as Regular Attendant of the Princely Domain of Wuling of Liang.
value.literal: Xingben first took office as Regular Attendant of the Princely Domain of Wuling of Liang.

value.zh: 遇蕭脩以梁州北附，遂與叔父璠歸周，寓居新豐。
value.en: When Xiao Xiu brought Liang Province north to submit, he returned to Zhou together with his uncle Fan and made his home in Xinfeng.
value.literal: When Xiao Xiu brought Liang Province north to submit, he then returned to Zhou together with his uncle Fan and lodged in Xinfeng.

value.zh: 每以諷讀為事，精力忘疲，雖衣食乏絕，晏如也。
value.en: He always made recitation and reading his occupation, driving himself without fatigue; though food and clothing ran short, he remained perfectly at ease.
value.literal: He always made recitation and reading his occupation, forgetting fatigue in his energy; though food and clothing were exhausted, he was perfectly at ease.

value.zh: 性剛烈，有不可奪之志。
value.en: By nature he was stern and resolute, with a will that could not be wrested away.
value.literal: By nature he was stern and resolute, with a will that could not be wrested away.

value.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外府記室。
value.en: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, summoned him as Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters.
value.literal: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, summoned him as Master of Records of the Central and Outer Headquarters.

value.zh: 武帝親總萬機，轉禦正中士，兼領起居注。
value.en: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Xingben was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently put in charge of the Daily Record.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Xingben was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Imperial Secretariat and concurrently put in charge of the Daily Record.

value.zh: 累遷掌朝下大夫。
value.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Court Attendance.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Court Attendance.

value.zh: 周代故事，天子臨軒，掌朝典筆硯，持至御坐，則承禦大夫取進之。
value.en: By Zhou custom, when the Son of Heaven faced the hall, the Court Attendance Master held the brush and inkstone and, on reaching the imperial seat, the Assistant Master of Attendance took them and presented them.
value.literal: By Zhou custom, when the Son of Heaven faced the hall, the Court Attendance Master held the brush and inkstone and, when he reached the imperial seat, the Assistant Master of Attendance took them and presented them.

value.zh: 及行本為掌朝，將進筆於帝，承禦復欲取之。
value.en: When Xingben was Court Attendance Master and was about to present the brush to the Emperor, the Assistant Master again tried to take it.
value.literal: When Xingben was Court Attendance Master and was about to present the brush to the Emperor, the Assistant Master again wished to take it.

value.zh: 行本抗聲曰：「筆不可得。」
value.en: Xingben said loudly, "The brush cannot be taken".
value.literal: Xingben said loudly: "The brush cannot be taken".

value.zh: 帝驚視問之，行本曰：「臣聞設官分職，各有司存。
value.en: The Emperor looked up in surprise and asked why; Xingben said, "I have heard that in establishing offices one divides duties, and each has its keeper.
value.literal: The Emperor looked up in surprise and asked why; Xingben said: "I have heard that in establishing offices one divides duties, and each has its keeper.

value.zh: 臣既不得佩承禦刀，承禦亦焉得取臣筆？」
value.en: Since I may not wear the Assistant Master's knife at my belt, how may the Assistant Master take my brush?"
value.literal: Since I may not wear the Assistant Master's knife at my belt, how may the Assistant Master take my brush?"

value.zh: 帝曰：「然。」
value.en: The Emperor said, "So it is."
value.literal: The Emperor said: "So it is."

value.zh: 因令二司各行所職。
value.en: He therefore ordered the two offices each to perform its own duty.
value.literal: He therefore ordered the two offices each to perform its own duty.

value.zh: 及宣帝嗣位，多失德，行本切諫忤旨，出為河內太守。
value.en: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne and often lost virtue, Xingben remonstrated sharply and offended the imperial will; he was sent out as Administrator of Henei.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne and often lost virtue, Xingben remonstrated sharply and offended the imperial will; he was sent out as Administrator of Henei.

value.zh: 及尉遲迥作亂，攻懷州，行本率吏人拒之，拜儀同，賜爵文安縣子。
value.en: When Wei Chijiong rebelled and attacked Huaizhou, Xingben led clerks and people to resist him; he was granted ceremonial parity and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an.
value.literal: When Wei Chijiong rebelled and attacked Huaizhou, Xingben led clerks and people to resist him; he was appointed with ceremonial parity and enfeoffed as Viscount of Wen'an.

value.zh: 王昌一名郎，趙國邯鄲人也。
value.en: Wang Chang, who also went by the name Wang Lang, came from Handan in Zhao.
value.literal: Wang Chang, another name Lang, was a man of Handan in the state of Zhao.

value.zh: 素為卜相工，明星曆，常以為河北有天子氣。
value.en: He made his living reading omens and faces, knew the stars and the calendar, and had long been convinced that the region north of the river bore the portents of an emperor.
value.literal: He had long worked as a diviner and physiognomist, understood the stars and calendars, and constantly believed that north of the Yellow River there was the aura of a Son of Heaven.

value.zh: 時趙繆王子林，景帝七代孫也，好奇數，任俠於趙、魏間，多通豪猾，而郎與之親善。
value.en: At the time Liu Lin, a son of Prince Miao of Zhao and a seventh-generation descendant of Emperor Jing, delighted in strange numerological arts, acted as a bravo between Zhao and Wei, and had many ties with powerful scoundrels; Wang Lang was close to him.
value.literal: At the time Liu Lin, a son of Prince Miao of Zhao and a seventh-generation descendant of Emperor Jing, delighted in strange numerological arts, acted as a bravo between Zhao and Wei, and had many ties with powerful scoundrels; Wang Lang was close to him.

value.zh: 初，王莽篡位，長安中或自稱成帝子子輿者，莽殺之。
value.en: After Wang Mang usurped the throne, a man in Chang’an had claimed to be Ziyu, a son of Emperor Cheng; Mang had him executed.
value.literal: Earlier, when Wang Mang seized the throne, someone in Chang’an who called himself Ziyu, a son of Emperor Cheng, was killed by Mang.

value.zh: 郎緣是詐稱真子輿，云『母故成帝謳者，嘗下殿卒僵，須臾有黃氣從上下，半日乃解，遂妊身就館。
value.en: Wang Lang therefore passed himself off as the genuine Liu Ziyu, claiming: "My mother was once a palace singer to Emperor Cheng. She once came down from the hall and suddenly collapsed; after a little while yellow vapor flowed down from above, and only after half a day did she recover. She then conceived and was sent to the birth house.
value.literal: Lang on this account falsely called himself the true Ziyu, saying: ‘My mother had been a singer for Emperor Cheng; once when descending the hall she suddenly collapsed stiff; in a moment yellow vapour came from above and below; only after half a day did she recover, and then she was pregnant and went to the lying-in quarters.

value.zh: 趙後欲害之，偽易他人子，以故得全。
value.en: Empress Zhao tried to destroy me, but another person's child was substituted as a deception, and so I was preserved.
value.literal: Empress Zhao wished to harm him; she falsely exchanged another person’s child; by this means he was preserved whole.

value.zh: 子輿年十二，識命者郎中李曼卿，與俱至蜀；
value.en: At twelve, Ziyu met the physiognomist and court gentleman Li Manqing and traveled with him into Shu;
value.literal: When Ziyu was twelve, he met the fate-reader Gentleman-of-the-Palace Li Manqing and together with him went to Shu.

value.zh: 十七，到丹陽；
value.en: at seventeen, he reached Danyang;
value.literal: At seventeen, he arrived at Danyang.

value.zh: 二十，還長安；
value.en: at twenty, he returned to Chang'an;
value.literal: At twenty, he returned to Chang’an.

value.zh: 展轉中山，來往燕、趙，以須天時』。
value.en: then he drifted through Zhongshan and between Yan and Zhao, waiting for Heaven's time."
value.literal: He shifted to Zhongshan, coming and going between Yan and Zhao, in order to await the heavenly season.’

value.zh: 林等愈動疑惑，乃與趙國大豪李育、張參等通謀，規共立郎。
value.en: The story unsettled Liu Lin and his circle; they conspired with Zhao notables Li Yu and Zhang Can to set Wang Lang on the throne.
value.literal: Lin and the others were increasingly moved to doubt, and then with great magnates of Zhao such as Li Yu and Zhang Can secretly plotted, planning together to establish Lang.

value.zh: 會人間傳赤眉將度河，林等因此宣言赤眉當立劉子輿以觀眾心，百姓多信之。
value.en: When word among the people spread that the Red Eyebrows were about to cross the Yellow River, Liu Lin and the others used this to declare that the Red Eyebrows would establish Liu Ziyu, in order to observe the public mood; many commoners believed it.
value.literal: When word among the people spread that the Red Eyebrows were about to cross the Yellow River, Liu Lin and the others used this to declare that the Red Eyebrows would establish Liu Ziyu, in order to observe the public mood; many commoners believed it.

value.zh: 更始敗，三水豪傑共計議，以芳劉氏子孫，宜承宗廟，乃共立芳為上將軍、西平王，欲平定西方，故以為號。
value.en: When Gengshi was defeated, the powerful men of Sanshui deliberated together and, because Fang was a descendant of the Liu clan and ought to inherit the ancestral temples, they jointly set up Fang as Supreme General and King of Xiping. They wanted to pacify the west, and therefore used that as his title.
value.literal: When Gengshi was defeated, the powerful men of Sanshui deliberated together and, because Fang was a descendant of the Liu clan and ought to inherit the ancestral temples, they jointly set up Fang as Supreme General and King of Xiping. They wanted to pacify the west, and therefore used that as his title.

value.zh: 單于曰：「匈奴本與漢約為兄弟。
value.en: The chanyu said, “The Xiongnu originally made a covenant with the Han to be brothers.
value.literal: The chanyu said, “The Xiongnu originally made a covenant with the Han to be brothers.

value.zh: 後匈奴中衰，呼韓邪單于歸漢，漢為發兵擁護，世世稱臣。
value.en: Later, when the Xiongnu waned, Chanyu Huhanye submitted to Han; Han sent armies to shield him, and for generations his people called themselves vassals.
value.literal: Later the Xiongnu middle declined; Shanyu Huhanye returned to Han; Han for him raised troops to protect; generation after generation called themselves ministers.

value.zh: 今漢亦中絕，劉氏來歸我，亦當立之，令尊事我。』
value.en: Now Han’s line is broken; the Lius come to me for shelter—I should set one of them up and make him honour my authority.’
value.literal: Now Han also is cut off in the middle; the Liu clan comes to submit to me; I also ought to establish him, order him to honour and serve me.

value.zh: 乃使句林王將數千騎迎芳，芳與兄禽、弟程俱入匈奴。
value.en: He sent the Goulin king with thousands of riders to escort Lu Fang; Lu Fang entered the steppe with his brothers Qin and Cheng.
value.literal: ’ Thereupon he ordered the Goulin King to lead several thousand cavalry to welcome Fang; Fang together with elder brother Qin, younger brother Cheng, all entered the Xiongnu.

value.zh: 單于遂立芳為漢帝。
value.en: The chanyu thereupon proclaimed him emperor of Han.
value.literal: The Shanyu thereupon established Fang as Han emperor.

value.zh: 以程為中郎將，將胡騎還入安定。
value.en: He made Cheng a gentleman of the palace and sent him back into Anding at the head of Hu cavalry.
value.literal: He appointed Cheng as gentleman of the palace, led Hu cavalry back into Anding.

value.zh: 呼韓邪單于降漢，入朝，宣帝擁護，國內遂定。
value.en: When Huhanye Chanyu surrendered to Han and came to court, Emperor Xuan protected him, and order was then established within his state.
value.literal: When Huhanye Chanyu surrendered to Han and came to court, Emperor Xuan protected him, and order was then established within his state.

value.zh: 使使與西羌、匈奴結和親。
value.en: They sent envoys to form marriage alliances with the Western Qiang and the Xiongnu.
value.literal: They sent envoys to form marriage alliances with the Western Qiang and the Xiongnu.

value.zh: 高祖時，與冒頓單于約為兄弟。
value.en: In Gaozu’s time, he made a covenant with Maodun Chanyu to be brothers.
value.literal: In Gaozu’s time, he made a covenant with Maodun Chanyu to be brothers.

value.zh: 長伯，豐字也。
value.en: Changbo was Feng’s style name.
value.literal: Changbo was Feng’s style name.

value.zh: 豐，平帝時為少府，王莽篡位時為更始將軍。
value.en: Feng was Lesser Treasurer in Emperor Ping’s time and General Who Renews Beginnings when Wang Mang usurped the throne.
value.literal: Feng was Lesser Treasurer in Emperor Ping’s time and General Who Renews Beginnings when Wang Mang usurped the throne.

value.zh: 好奇數，術數。
value.en: Delighting in strange shu means in numerological arts.
value.literal: Delighting in strange shu means in numerological arts.

value.zh: 《王莽傳》曰，時男子武仲自稱劉子輿。
value.en: The Biography of Wang Mang says that at that time a man named Wu Zhong claimed to be Liu Ziyu.
value.literal: The Biography of Wang Mang says that at that time a man named Wu Zhong claimed to be Liu Ziyu.

value.zh: 趙飛燕也。
value.en: This was Zhao Feiyan.
value.literal: This was Zhao Feiyan.

value.zh: 《東觀記》曰：「宮婢生子，正與同時，即易之」也。
value.en: The Dongguan Record says, “A palace maid bore a child at exactly the same time, and he was then exchanged for that child.”
value.literal: The Dongguan Record says, “A palace maid bore a child at exactly the same time, and he was then exchanged for that child.”

value.zh: 識命謂知天命也。
value.en: Shiming, “recognizing destiny,” means knowing Heaven’s command.
value.literal: Shiming, “recognizing destiny,” means knowing Heaven’s command.

value.zh: 須，待也。
value.en: Xu means “to wait.”
value.literal: Xu means “to wait.”

value.zh: 耿弇字伯昭，扶風茂陵人也。
value.en: Geng Yan, courtesy name Bozhao, was a native of Maoling in Fufeng commandery.
value.literal: Geng Yan, styled Bozhao, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng.

value.zh: 其先武帝時以吏二千石自巨鹿徙焉。
value.en: His forebears had held a two-thousand-dan post under Emperor Wu and relocated from Julu to Maoling.
value.literal: His ancestors, in the time of Emperor Wu, as officials at the rank of two thousand shi, moved from Julu to there.

value.zh: 父況，字俠遊，以明經為郎，與王莽從弟伋共學《老子》於安丘先生，後為朔調連率。
value.en: His father Geng Kuang, courtesy name Xiayou, entered court as a gentleman-attendant on the strength of his classical learning; with Wang Mang's cousin Wang Ji he studied the Laozi under Master Anqiu, and was later appointed chain commandant of the Shuodiao circuit.
value.literal: His father Kuang, styled Xiayou, through understanding the classics became a gentleman-attendant, and with Wang Mang's cousin Ji together studied the Laozi under Master Anqiu, afterward became chain commandant of Shuodiao.

value.zh: 弇少好學，習父業。
value.en: From boyhood Geng Yan loved learning and followed his father's scholarly path.
value.literal: Yan in youth loved study, practiced his father's occupation.

value.zh: 常見郡尉試騎士，建旗鼓，肄馳射，由是好將帥之事。
value.en: He often watched the commandery commandant drill mounted archers—drums and banners raised, bows shot at full gallop—and so grew fond of the business of command.
value.literal: He often saw the commandery commandant test mounted knights, set up drums and banners, drill mounted archery, thereby came to love generals' and commanders' affairs.

value.zh: 是時，烏桓、鮮卑屢寇外境，國素有籌策，數言邊事，帝器之。
value.en: At that time the Wuhuan and Xianbei harried the frontier again and again; Geng Guo was full of stratagems, spoke often on border policy, and the emperor valued him.
value.literal: At this time, Wuhuan, Xianbei repeatedly raided outer borders, Guo always had plans, several times spoke border affairs, emperor esteemed him.

value.zh: 及匈奴薁日逐王比自立為呼韓邪單元，款塞稱藩，願扞禦北虜。
value.en: When the Xiongnu prince Bi, the Ailizhuyu king, set himself up as Chanyu in the manner of Huhanye, crossed the passes as a vassal, and offered to shield the north against other barbarians,
value.literal: When Xiongnu Ailizhuyu King Bi self-established as Chanyu Huhanye, opened barrier called vassal, wished defend north caitiffs.

value.zh: 事下公卿。
value.en: the matter was referred to the high ministers.
value.literal: Matter sent down to dukes and ministers.

value.zh: 議者皆以為天下初定，中國空虛，夷狄情偽難知，不可許。
value.en: The consensus was that the empire was newly pacified, the heartland still drained, and barbarian intentions impossible to read—the court should not agree.
value.literal: Debaters all thought empire first settled, central plain empty void, barbarians true-false hard know, not permissible grant.

value.zh: 國獨曰：『臣以為宜如孝宣故事受之，令東扞鮮卑，北拒匈奴，率厲四夷，完復邊郡，使塞下無晏開之警，萬世安寧之策也。』
value.en: Geng Guo alone said, 'I hold we should follow Emperor Xuan's precedent and accept him, set him to block the Xianbei on the east and hold the Xiongnu on the north, rally the four barbarians, restore the lost border commanderies, and keep the passes free of sudden alarms—that is the plan for peace for ages to come.'
value.literal: Guo alone said: 'Your subject thinks ought like Filial Emperor Xuan former case receive him, order east block Xianbei, north resist Xiongnu, lead encourage four barbarians, restore complete border commanderies, make below passes no late-opening alarm, ten thousand generations peace quiet plan.'

value.zh: 帝從其議，遂立比為南單于。
value.en: The emperor adopted his argument and established Bi as southern chanyu.
value.literal: Emperor followed his discussion, thereupon established Bi as South Chanyu.

value.zh: 由是烏桓、鮮卑保塞自守，北虜遠遁，中國少事。
value.en: Thereafter the Wuhuan and Xianbei guarded the line for themselves, the northern raiders withdrew far away, and the heartland knew less trouble.
value.literal: Thereby Wuhuan, Xianbei guarded passes self-defend, north caitiffs far fled, central plain few affairs.

value.zh: 二十七年，代馮勤為大司農。
value.en: In the twenty-seventh year he succeeded Feng Qin as grand minister of agriculture.
value.literal: Twenty-seventh year, replaced Feng Qin as grand minister of agriculture.

value.zh: 又上言宜置度遼將軍、左右校尉，屯五原以防逃亡。
value.en: He further memorialized that a general-across-the-Liao and left and right colonels should be posted with a garrison at Wuyuan to check desertions.
value.literal: Again submitted memorial saying ought establish general who crosses the Liao, left and right colonels, garrison Wuyuan to guard against fugitives.

value.zh: 永平元年卒官。
value.en: He died in office in the first year of Yongping.
value.literal: Yongping first year died in office.

value.zh: 顯宗追思國言，後遂置度遼將軍、左右校尉，如其議焉。
value.en: Emperor Ming later remembered Geng Guo's counsel and eventually did institute the general-across-the-Liao and the left and right colonels as he had proposed.
value.literal: Emperor Ming afterward recalled Guo's words, later then established general who crosses the Liao, left and right colonels, as his discussion.

value.zh: 恭字伯宗，國弟廣之子也。
value.en: Geng Gong, courtesy name Bozong, was the son of Geng Guo's younger brother Geng Guang.
value.literal: Gong styled Bozong, was Guo's younger brother Guang's son.

value.zh: 少孤。
value.en: He was orphaned while young.
value.literal: In youth orphaned.

value.zh: 慷慨多大略，有將帥才。
value.en: He was high-minded and far-sighted, with a born commander's gifts.
value.literal: Stirred generous had great plans, had generals' and commanders' talent.

value.zh: 永平十七年冬，騎都尉劉張出擊車師，請恭為司馬，與奉車都尉竇固及從弟駙馬都尉秉破降之。
value.en: In the winter of the seventeenth year of Yongping, when Cavalry Commandant Liu Zhang marched against Jushi, he asked for Geng Gong as his major; with Coach Commandant Dou Gu and his cousin Coach Commandant Geng Bing they crushed and received the surrender of Jushi.
value.literal: Yongping seventeenth year winter, cavalry commandant Liu Zhang exited strike Jushi, requested Gong as major, with coach commandant Dou Gu and cousin coach commandant Bing broke and surrendered them.

value.zh: 始置西域都護、戊己校尉，乃以恭為戊己校尉，屯後王部金蒲城，謁者關寵為戊己校尉，屯前王柳中城，屯各置數百人。
value.en: When the protector-general of the Western Regions and the Wu and Ji colonels were first instituted, Geng Gong was named colonel of Wu and Ji and stationed with the rear king's people at Jinfu, while the herald Guan Chong was named colonel of Wu and Ji and stationed at Liuzhong with the front king; each garrison held several hundred men.
value.literal: First established Western Regions protector, Wu and Ji colonels, then made Gong Wu and Ji colonel, garrisoned rear king's division at Jinfu city, herald Guan Chong as Wu and Ji colonel, garrisoned front king's Liuzhong city, garrisons each placed several hundred men.

value.zh: 恭至部，移檄烏孫，示漢威德，大昆彌以下皆歡喜，遣使獻名馬，及奉宣帝時所賜公主博具，願遣子入侍。
value.en: When Geng Gong reached his command he sent a manifesto to Wusun proclaiming Han might and virtue; the great Kunmi and his court rejoiced, sent envoys with famous horses, returned the board games given the princess under Emperor Xuan, and asked to send a son to court.
value.literal: Gong reached division, transmitted proclamation Wusun, displayed Han might and virtue, great Kunmi down all rejoiced, dispatched envoys presented famous horses, and offered Emperor Xuan-time bestowed princess board games, wished send son enter attend.

value.zh: 恭乃發使賫金帛，迎其侍子。
value.en: Geng Gong then sent envoys with gold and silks to escort the hostage prince.
value.literal: Gong then dispatched envoys carrying gold silks, welcome his attendant son.

value.zh: 楊終字子山，蜀郡成都人也。
value.en: Yang Zhong, styled Zishan, came from Chengdu in Shu commandery.
value.literal: Yang Zhong, courtesy name Zishan, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

value.zh: 年十三，為郡小吏，太守奇其才，遣詣京師受業，習春秋。
value.en: When he was thirteen he served as a junior clerk in the commandery. The grand administrator, struck by his ability, sent him to the capital for schooling, and there he mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals.
value.literal: At age thirteen he became a petty clerk in the commandery; the grand administrator marveled at his talent and sent him to the capital to study, where he learned the Chunqiu.

value.zh: [一]顯宗時，征詣蘭台，拜校書郎。
value.en: Under Emperor Ming he was called to the Orchid Terrace and given the post of collating secretary [1].
value.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming [note 1], he was summoned to the Orchid Terrace and appointed collator.

value.zh: 終又言：「宣帝博征群儒，論定五經於石渠閣。
value.en: Zhong also said: "Emperor Xuan widely summoned Confucian scholars and fixed the meaning of the Five Classics in the Stone Canal Pavilion.
value.literal: Zhong also said: "Emperor Xuan widely summoned Confucian scholars and fixed the meaning of the Five Classics in the Stone Canal Pavilion.

value.zh: 方今天下少事，學者得成其業，而章句之徒，破壞大體。
value.en: Today, with few disturbances in the empire, learners could perfect their craft, but petty exegetes are tearing apart the larger tradition.
value.literal: Now the realm has few troubles and students can complete their studies, yet the chapter-and-verse crowd ruin the great pattern.

value.zh: 宜如石渠故事，永為後世則。」
value.en: He proposed repeating the Stone Canal conference so as to leave a permanent standard for posterity."
value.literal: It would be fitting to follow the Stone Canal precedent and make a lasting model for later ages."

value.zh: 於是詔諸儒於白虎觀論考同異焉。
value.en: An edict followed, summoning Confucians to the White Tiger Hall to thrash out textual agreement and disagreement.
value.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the scholars to debate agreements and differences at the White Tiger Hall.

value.zh: 會終坐事系獄，博士趙博、校書郎班固、賈逵等，以終深曉春秋，學多異聞，表請之，終又上書自訟，即日貰出，乃得與於白虎觀焉。
value.en: When Yang Zhong was jailed for a separate matter, Zhao Bo, Ban Gu, Jia Kui, and others petitioned that his mastery of the Annals and wide learning deserved mercy; his own memorial won him a pardon that very day, and he joined the White Tiger deliberations.
value.literal: It happened that Zhong was imprisoned for an offense; Erudite Zhao Bo, collator Ban Gu, Jia Kui, and others, because Zhong thoroughly understood the Chunqiu and had learned many unusual traditions, memorialized for him; Zhong also submitted a memorial in his own defense, and the same day he was pardoned and released, and so was able to take part in the White Tiger conference.

value.zh: [一]後受詔刪太史公書為十餘萬言。
value.en: He was later commissioned to condense Sima Qian's history to more than one hundred thousand characters.
value.literal: Later he received orders to abridge the Grand Scribe's book to over a hundred thousand characters.

value.zh: 左雄字伯豪，南*
value.en: Zuo Xiong, whose courtesy name was Bohao, came from Nanyang commandery
value.literal: Zuo Xiong, courtesy name Bohao, was a native of Nanyang

value.en: (the commandery name)
value.literal: (commandery)

value.zh: **[陽]*涅陽人也。
value.en: specifically of Nieyang.
value.literal: [Yang]—of Nieyang.

value.zh: 安帝時，舉孝廉，稍遷冀州刺史。
value.en: During the reign of Emperor An, he was nominated as filial and incorrupt and rose step by step to the governorship of Ji Province.
value.literal: Under Emperor An, he was recommended as filial and incorrupt, and was gradually promoted to Governor of Ji Province.

value.zh: 州部多豪族，好請托，雄常閉門不與交通。
value.en: The region was full of powerful families who habitually pulled strings; Zuo Xiong routinely kept his gate closed and refused such traffic.
value.literal: The province abounded in powerful clans who loved to seek favors through connections; Xiong often shut his doors and had no dealings with them.

value.zh: 奏案貪猾二千石，無所回忌。
value.en: He impeached and prosecuted venal and evasive prefects and commandery governors, showing neither hesitation nor favor.
value.literal: He memorialized to investigate corrupt and slippery two-thousand-dan officials, without any turning back or scruple.

value.zh: 故其詩云：「四國無政，不用其良。」
value.en: Hence the Poetry laments: "Throughout the four quarters there is no sound rule; the good are not employed."
value.literal: Therefore its Odes says: "In the four states there is no good government; they do not use their good men."

value.zh: 又曰：「哀今之人，胡為虺蜴？」
value.en: It adds: "Pity the people of this age—why are they treated like poisonous snakes and lizards?"
value.literal: It also says: "Alas for the people of today—why are they like vipers and lizards?"

value.zh: 言人畏吏如虺蜴也。
value.en: The point is that the people dread magistrates as they would venomous reptiles.
value.literal: It means people fear officials like vipers and lizards.

value.zh: [四]宗周既滅，六國並秦，坑儒泯典，僄革五等，更立郡縣，[五] 縣設令長，郡置守尉，什伍相司，封豕其民。
value.en: [4] After Western Zhou fell and the six states were swallowed by Qin, the First Emperor buried scholars alive and burned the classics, abolished the feudal grades, and replaced them with commanderies and counties; [5] each county had a magistrate, each commandery a governor and commandant, and the mutual-surveillance groups of households penned the people in like hogs for the slaughter.
value.literal: [4] When the Zhou of the west was destroyed, the six states were annexed by Qin; it buried the scholars and extinguished the canons; it drastically cut away the five ranks and instead established commanderies and counties; [5] counties had magistrates and elders, commanderies had governors and commandants; the ten-and-five households watched one another; it treated its people like a great boar.

value.zh: [六]大漢受命，雖未復古，然克慎庶官，蠲苛救敝，悅以濟難，撫而循之。
value.en: [6] When Han received Heaven's charge it did not fully revive the old order, yet it was scrupulous about offices, lifted oppressive laws, and nursed the realm through hardship with kindness and restraint.
value.literal: [6] When the great Han received the mandate, although it did not fully restore antiquity, yet it was able to be careful with the multitude of offices, abolish harshness and rescue what was flawed, please the people to cross difficulties, and soothe and follow them.

value.zh: 至於文、景，天下康乂。
value.en: By the reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing the empire was secure and orderly.
value.literal: As for Wen and Jing, the realm was peaceful and well-governed.

value.zh: 誠由玄靖寬柔，克慎官人故也。
value.en: This was due to their deep calm, their gentle rule, and their care in choosing officials.
value.literal: Truly it was because of profound quietness, lenient softness, and being able to be careful in appointing men.

value.zh: 降及宣帝，興於仄陋，綜核名實，知時所病，刺史守相，輒親引見，考察言行，信賞必罰。
value.en: Down to Emperor Xuan, who had risen from obscurity, who matched names to deeds and grasped what ailed the age—when he dealt with regional inspectors, governors, and chancellors he would call them in himself, weigh word against deed, and never waver on reward or punishment.
value.literal: Descending to Emperor Xuan, who rose from a humble corner, he comprehensively examined names and realities, knew the ills of the times, and for governors and shepherds and ministers he would personally summon and interview them, investigate their words and deeds, and in rewards and punishments was trustworthy and certain.

value.zh: 帝乃歎曰：「民所以安而無怨者，政平吏良也。
value.en: The emperor once sighed and said, "The people live untroubled and without complaint because policy is fair and the magistrates are good.
value.literal: The Emperor then sighed, saying: "The reason the people are peaceful and without resentment is that government is even and officials are good.

value.zh: 注[七]宣帝時鳳皇五至，因以紀年。
value.en: Note [7]: under Emperor Xuan the phoenix appeared five times, and reign titles commemorated it.
value.literal: Note [7] In Emperor Xuan's time phoenixes came five times, and thereby years were recorded.

value.zh: 夫子聽衛國之政，修其班制，不亦文乎？
value.en: He put Wei's government in order—is that not refinement?
value.literal: The master heard Wei's government, cultivated its ranks and regulations—is this not cultured?

value.zh: 謂夫子『貞惠文子』。」
value.en: Call him the Loyal, Kind, Refined Master.
value.literal: We call the master 'Loyal, Kindly, Cultured Master.'

value.zh: 事見禮記。
value.en: The story is in the Book of Rites.
value.literal: The affair is seen in the Record of Rites.

value.zh: 尹翁歸為右扶風，*[卒]*，宣帝下詔□揚，賜金百斤。
value.en: Yin Wengui, governor of You Fufeng, died in office; Emperor Xuan issued an edict of praise and sent a hundred jin of gold.
value.literal: Yin Wengui was Governor of You Fufeng; [when he died], Emperor Xuan issued an edict [lacuna] praising him and bestowed one hundred jin of gold.

value.zh: 班固曰：「翁歸承風，帝揚厥聲。」
value.en: Ban Gu wrote, "Wengui caught the imperial breeze, and the throne magnified his name."
value.literal: Ban Gu says: "Wengui received the wind; the Emperor raised his fame."

value.zh: 故曰蒙述也。
value.en: Hence the phrase that the throne "spread his fame" in a written tribute.
value.literal: Therefore it is said he received narrative.

value.zh: 安平獻王孚
value.en: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.
value.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).

value.zh: 孚雖見尊寵，不以為榮，常有憂色。
value.en: Yet privilege brought him no joy—his face stayed shadowed with worry.
value.literal: Though Fu saw honor and favor he did not regard it as glory and often wore a troubled expression.

value.zh: 臨終，遺令曰：「有魏貞士河內溫縣司馬孚，字叔達，不伊不周，不夷不惠，立身行道，終始若一，當以素棺單槨，斂以時服。」
value.en: At his deathbed his testament said, 'There was a Wei loyalist of Henei Wen county, Sima Fu, courtesy Shuda—not acting Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou, neither withdrawing like Boyi nor compromising like Liuxiahui—who established himself and walked the Way from first to last as one; bury me in an unvarnished coffin with a single-layer outer shell and dress me in timely ordinary clothes.'
value.literal: At his deathbed his testament said, 'There was a Wei loyalist of Henei Wen county, Sima Fu, courtesy Shuda—not acting Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou, neither withdrawing like Boyi nor compromising like Liuxiahui—who established himself and walked the Way from first to last as one; bury me in an unvarnished coffin with a single-layer outer shell and dress me in timely ordinary clothes.'

value.zh: 泰始八年薨，時年九十三。
value.en: He died in the eighth year of Taishi at ninety-three.
value.literal: He died in the eighth year of Taishi at ninety-three.

value.zh: 帝於太極東堂舉哀三日。
value.en: Emperor Wu mourned three days in Taiji's east hall.
value.literal: The emperor observed mourning three days in the eastern hall of Taiji Palace.

value.zh: 詔曰：「王勳德超世，尊寵無二，期頤在位，朕之所倚。
value.en: An edict said, 'The prince's merit and virtue surpass the age; honor and favor were without peer; he dwelt in office at a hundred years—what I relied upon.
value.literal: An edict said, 'The prince's merit and virtue surpass the age; honor and favor were without peer; he dwelt in office at a hundred years—what I relied upon.

value.zh: 庶永百齡，諮仰訓導，奄忽殂隕，哀慕感切。
value.en: I hoped he would last forever to consult and look up to his instruction—suddenly he has fallen and passed away; grief and longing cut deep.
value.literal: I hoped he would last forever to consult and look up to his instruction—suddenly he has fallen and passed away; grief and longing cut deep.

value.zh: 其以東園溫明秘器、朝服一具、衣一襲、緋練百匹、絹布各五百匹、錢百萬，穀千斛以供喪事。
value.en: Let there be supplied for the funeral the eastern park warming coffin and secret fittings, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, one hundred bolts of crimson silk, five hundred bolts each of silk and cloth, a million cash, and a thousand hu of grain.
value.literal: Let there be supplied for the funeral the eastern park warming coffin and secret fittings, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, one hundred bolts of crimson silk, five hundred bolts each of silk and cloth, a million cash, and a thousand hu of grain.

value.zh: 諸所施行，皆依漢東平獻王蒼故事。」
value.en: All measures implemented shall follow the precedent of Han Prince Xian of Dongping, Liu Cang."
value.literal: All measures implemented shall follow the precedent of Han Prince Xian of Dongping, Liu Cang."

value.zh: 其家遵孚遺旨，所給器物，一不施用。
value.en: The clan honored his will and refused every gifted token.
value.literal: His family obeyed Fu's testamentary instructions; not one of the supplied implements was used.

value.zh: 帝再臨喪，親拜盡哀。
value.en: Sima Yan returned twice to bow in deepest sorrow.
value.literal: The emperor twice attended the mourning and personally bowed in full grief.

value.zh: 及葬，又幸都亭，望柩而拜，哀動左右。
value.en: At interment he halted at the post station, bowed toward the catafalque, and moved every witness.
value.literal: When it came to burial he also went to the courier station, gazed toward the bier and bowed, moving those around him to grief.

value.zh: 給鑾輅輕車，介士武賁百人，吉凶導從二千餘人，前後鼓吹，配饗太廟。
value.en: The cortège drew imperial hearses, a hundred household guards, two thousand ushers, full musical escort, and enshrinement beside the royal ancestors.
value.literal: There were provided imperial escort carriages and light wagons, one hundred armored guards and palace runners, over two thousand attendants for auspicious and inauspicious processions, front and rear trumpets and drums, and joint sacrifice in the Grand Temple.

value.zh: 九子：邕、望、輔、翼、晃、瑰、珪、衡、景。
value.en: He had nine sons named Yong, Wang, Fu, Yi, Huang, Gui, Gui, Heng, and Jing—the fifth and sixth homophonous but written with different graphs.
value.literal: Nine sons: Yong, Wang, Fu, Yi, Huang, Gui (lapis), Gui (jade tablet), Heng, Jing.

value.zh: 吳將施績寇江夏，邊境騷動。
value.en: Wu general Shi Ji's strike on Jiangxia threw the frontier into alarm.
value.literal: Wu general Shi Ji raided Jiangxia and the border was disturbed.

value.zh: 以望統中軍步騎二萬，出屯龍陂，為二方重鎮，假節，加大都督諸軍事。
value.en: Wang led twenty thousand central troops to Longpi as the brace between two theaters, credentials in hand as grand commander.
value.literal: Wang was ordered to command twenty thousand infantry and cavalry of the central army, go out and encamp at Longpi as heavy garrison for two fronts, given credentials, and additionally promoted grand commander of all military affairs.

value.zh: 會荊州刺史胡烈距績，破之，望乃班師。
value.en: When Jing inspector Hu Lie routed Shi Ji, Wang stood down his army.
value.literal: It happened that Inspector of Jing Province Hu Lie resisted Ji and defeated him; thereupon Wang withdrew the army.

value.zh: 俄而吳將丁奉寇芍陂，望又率諸軍以赴之，未至而奉退。
value.en: Ding Feng's raid on Quepi drew Wang east again, though the enemy slipped away before he arrived.
value.literal: Soon Wu general Ding Feng raided Quepi; Wang again led the various armies to hurry there; before he arrived Feng withdrew.

value.zh: 拜大司馬。
value.en: He received appointment as grand marshal.
value.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal.

value.zh: 孫皓率眾向壽春，詔望統中軍二萬，騎三千，據淮北。
value.en: Sun Hao's thrust toward Shouchun sent Wang to the north bank of the Huai with twenty thousand foot and three thousand horse.
value.literal: Sun Hao led a host toward Shouchun; an edict ordered Wang to command twenty thousand central troops and three thousand cavalry and hold north of the Huai.

value.zh: 皓退，軍罷。
value.en: Sun Hao withdrew and the mobilization ended.
value.literal: Hao withdrew and the army was disbanded.

value.zh: 泰始七年薨，時年六十七，賻贈有加，望性儉吝而好聚斂，身亡之後，金帛盈溢，以此獲譏。
value.en: In the seventh year of Taishi, he died at sixty-seven amid lavish obsequies yet earned ridicule for having hoarded treasure despite a miserly reputation.
value.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi, he died at age sixty-seven; funeral gifts were generous in addition; Wang's nature was frugal and stingy yet fond of amassing; after his death gold and silk overflowed; on this account he incurred ridicule.

value.zh: 四子：弈、洪、整、楙。
value.en: Four sons survived him: Yi, Hong, Zheng, and Mao.
value.literal: Four sons: Yi, Hong, Zheng, Mao.

value.zh: 河間平王洪，字孔業，出繼叔父昌武亭侯遺。
value.en: Sima Hong, Prince Ping of Hejian, styled Kongye, was adopted into uncle Yi's Changwu ting line.
value.literal: Prince Ping of Hejian, Hong, courtesy Kongye, went out to succeed uncle Marquis of Changwu precinct Yi.

value.zh: 仕魏，歷位典農中郎將、原武太守，封襄賁男。
value.en: Under Wei he served as agrarian colonel, Yuanwu governor, and baron of Xiangben.
value.literal: Serving Wei he successively held Agrarian Commandant, governor of Yuanwu, and was enfeoffed Baron of Xiangben.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，封河間王。
value.en: When Sima Yan took the throne Hong became prince of Hejian.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he was enfeoffed Prince of Hejian.

value.zh: 立十二年，咸寧二年薨。
value.en: After twelve years in the position, he died in Xianning year two.
value.literal: After twelve years in the position, he died in Xianning year two.

value.zh: 二子：威、混。
value.en: He left two sons, Wei and Hun.
value.literal: Two sons: Wei and Hun.

value.zh: 威嗣，徙封章武。
value.en: Wei inherited and moved the fief to Zhangwu.
value.literal: Wei succeeded and was transferred enfeoffment to Zhangwu.

value.zh: 其後威既繼義陽王望，更立混為洪嗣。
value.en: Once Wei continued Sima Wang's Yiyang title, Hun was designated Hong's heir.
value.literal: Later when Wei had succeeded Prince of Yiyang Wang, Hun was further established as Hong's successor.

value.zh: 混歷位散常侍，薨。
value.en: Hun served as supernumerary cavalry attendant and died.
value.literal: Hun successively held irregular attendant posts and died.

value.zh: 敬王恬，字元愉，少拜散騎侍郎，累遷散騎常侍、黃門郎、御史中丞。
value.en: Sima Tian rose through palace attendant posts to censor-in-chief.
value.literal: Prince Jing Tian courtesy Yuanyu youth appointed irregular cavalry gentleman progressively irregular cavalry attendant yellow-gate gentleman palace Assistant chief.

value.zh: 值海西廢，簡文帝登阼，未解嚴，大司馬桓溫屯中堂，吹警角，恬奏劾溫大不敬，請科罪。
value.en: Before demobilization Tian impeached Huan Wen's trumpet fanfare as lèse-majesté.
value.literal: When Haixi was deposed Emperor Jianwen ascended throne martial law not yet lifted Grand Marshal Huan Wen encamped Central Hall sounding alarm horns Tian memorialized impeaching Wen greatly irreverent requesting sentencing crime.

value.zh: 溫視奏歎曰：「此兒乃敢彈我，真可畏也。」
value.en: Wen viewing memorial sighed saying 'This lad dares impeach me—truly formidable.'
value.literal: Wen viewing memorial sighed saying 'This lad dares impeach me—truly formidable.'

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
value.en: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

value.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
value.en: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.
value.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

value.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
value.en: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
value.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

value.zh: 惠帝乃止。
value.en: Hui broke off his greeting.
value.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
value.en: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
value.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

value.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
value.en: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
value.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

value.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
value.en: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
value.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

value.zh: 由是奇之。
value.en: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.
value.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.

value.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
value.en: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
value.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'

value.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
value.en: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.
value.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

value.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」
value.en: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."
value.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'

value.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。
value.en: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
value.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

value.zh: 邵續
value.en: Shao Xu
value.literal: Shao Xu

value.zh: 邵續，字嗣祖，魏郡安陽人也。
value.en: Shao Xu, courtesy Sizu, came from Anyang in Wei Commandery.
value.literal: Shao Xu, style name Sizu, was a man of Anyang in Wei Commandery.

value.zh: 父乘，散騎侍郎。
value.en: His father, Shao Cheng, had risen to gentleman attendant at leisure.
value.literal: His father Shao Cheng was gentleman attendant at leisure.

value.zh: 續樸素有志烈，博覽經史，善談理義，妙解天文。
value.en: Shao Xu lived plainly and held fierce convictions; he read deeply across the classics and histories, argued principle with ease, and read the stars with uncommon skill.
value.literal: Shao Xu was plain and frugal and possessed of fierce resolve; he read widely in the classics and histories, was skilled at discussing principle and meaning, and had a subtle grasp of astronomy.

value.zh: 初為成都王穎參軍，穎將討長沙王乂，續諫曰：「續聞兄弟如左右手，今明公當天下之敵，而欲去一手乎？
value.en: He first joined the staff of Prince Chengdu, Sima Ying. When Ying prepared to strike Prince Changsha, Sima Yi, Shao Xu urged him: "They say brothers are like a man's two hands; you stand against the whole realm—would you willingly cut one off?
value.literal: At first he served as army adviser to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; when Ying was about to campaign against Prince Changsha Sima Yi, Shao Xu remonstrated: "I have heard that brothers are like the left and right hand; now the enlightened lord faces the empire's foes—would you wish to remove one hand?

value.zh: 續竊惑之。」
value.en: He could not fathom Ying's plan."
value.literal: Shao Xu privately was perplexed by this."

value.zh: 穎不納。
value.en: Ying would not listen.
value.literal: Ying did not accept it.

value.zh: 後為苟晞參軍，除沁水令。
value.en: He later served on Gou Xi's staff and was named magistrate of Qinshui.
value.literal: Later he served as army adviser to Gou Xi and was appointed magistrate of Qinshui.

value.zh: 四川土司諸境，多有去蜀遠，去滇、黔近者。
value.en: Many of the Sichuan tribal domains lay far from the Sichuan heartland but close to Yunnan and Guizhou.
value.literal: Of the various territories of the Sichuan tribal headmen, many are far from Shu yet close to Yunnan and Guizhou.

value.zh: 如烏蒙、東川近於滇，烏撒、鎮雄、播州近於黔。
value.en: Wumeng and Dongchuan lay near Yunnan, while Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Bozhou lay near Guizhou.
value.literal: For example, Wumeng and Dongchuan were close to Yunnan; Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Bozhou were close to Guizhou.

value.zh: 明太祖略定邊方，首平蜀夏，置四川布政司，使招諭諸蠻，次第歸附。
value.en: After the Hongwu Emperor had broadly secured the borderlands, he first conquered the Xia regime in Shu, set up the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission, and sent envoys to summon the various tribes to submit one after another.
value.literal: When the Hongwu Emperor had broadly pacified the frontier, he first subdued the Xia regime in Shu, established the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission, and sent envoys to summon and instruct the various barbarian peoples to submit in turn.

value.zh: 故烏蒙、烏撒、東川、芒部舊屬雲南者，皆隸於四川，不過歲輸貢賦，示以羈縻。
value.en: Thus Wumeng, Wusa, Dongchuan, and Mangbu, formerly part of Yunnan, were all placed under Sichuan jurisdiction, paying only annual tribute as a token of loose imperial control.
value.literal: Therefore Wumeng, Wusa, Dongchuan, and Mangbu, which had formerly belonged to Yunnan, were all placed under Sichuan—nothing more than annual tribute payments to display loose reins.

value.zh: 然夷性獷悍，嗜利好殺，爭相競尚，焚燒劫掠，習以為恒。
value.en: Yet the tribes were fierce by nature, greedy for profit and quick to kill; they competed in prestige, and burning, looting, and raiding had become their habitual way of life.
value.literal: Yet the barbarians were by nature fierce and violent, greedy for gain and fond of killing; they vied with one another in emulation, burning, plundering, and raiding as a constant practice.

value.zh: 去省窎遠，莫能控制，附近邊民，鹹被其毒。
value.en: So remote from the provincial seat that the government could not restrain them, they poisoned the lives of nearby border populations.
value.literal: Being far from the provincial capital, they could not be controlled, and neighboring border people all suffered their harm.

value.zh: 皆由規模草創，未嘗設立文武為之鈐轄，聽其自相雄長。
value.en: This arose because the system was still rudimentary: no civil or military officials had been stationed to keep them in check, and they were left to vie among themselves for dominance.
value.literal: All this was because the framework was newly established and no civil or military officials had been set up to exercise control, leaving them to contend among themselves for supremacy.

value.zh: 雖受天朝爵號，實自王其地。
value.en: Though they bore titles granted by the dynasty, in practice they ruled their own territories like kings.
value.literal: Although they received titles from the Celestial Court, in truth they were kings of their own lands.

value.zh: 以故終明之世，常煩撻伐。
value.en: Hence throughout the Ming period the court was repeatedly obliged to launch punitive expeditions against them.
value.literal: For this reason, throughout the Ming dynasty campaigns of suppression were constantly required.

value.zh: 唯建昌、松、茂等處設立衛所，播州改遵義、平越二府以後，稍安戢雲。
value.en: Only after guard posts were set up at Jianchang, Songpan, Maozhou, and elsewhere, and Bozhou was reorganized into the prefectures of Zunyi and Pingyue, did the region grow somewhat calmer.
value.literal: Only after guard posts were established at Jianchang, Songpan, Maozhou, and elsewhere, and after Bozhou was reorganized into the two prefectures of Zunyi and Pingyue, did the region grow somewhat more tranquil.

value.zh: 茂州，古冉駹國地。
value.en: Maozhou was ancient Ranrang territory.
value.literal: Maozhou was the land of the ancient Ranrang state.

value.zh: 漢武帝置汶山郡，宣帝為北部都尉。
value.en: Han Emperor Wu made Wenshan Commandery; Emperor Xuan a northern frontier command.
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Han established Wenshan Commandery; Emperor Xuan made it the northern frontier commandant's district.

value.zh: 隋為蜀州，尋改會州。
value.en: Sui: Shu Prefecture, soon Hui Prefecture.
value.literal: Under the Sui it was Shu Prefecture, soon changed to Hui Prefecture.

value.zh: 唐貞觀改茂州。
value.en: Tang Zhenguan: Maozhou.
value.literal: In the Zhenguan era of Tang it was changed to Maozhou.

value.zh: 宋、元仍舊，治汶山縣。
value.en: Song and Yuan kept the name and ruled from Wenshan County.
value.literal: Song and Yuan kept the old name, administering Wenshan County.

value.zh: 洪武六年，茂州權知州楊者七及隴木頭、靜州、嶽希蓬諸土官來朝貢。
value.en: Hongwu year 6: acting prefect Yang Zheqi and chiefs of Longmutou, Jingzhou, and Yuexipeng presented tribute.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu the acting prefect Yang Zheqi and the native officials of Longmutou, Jingzhou, and Yuexipeng came to court with tribute.

value.zh: 十一年置茂州衛指揮使司。
value.en: Year 11: Maozhou Guard was founded.
value.literal: In the eleventh year the Maozhou Guard command was established.

value.zh: 時四川都司遣兵修灌縣橋梁至陶關，汶川土酋孟道貴疑之，集部落阻陶關道。
value.en: Sichuan troops repairing the Guanxian bridge to Taoguan alarmed Wenchuan chief Meng Daogui, who blocked the road.
value.literal: At that time the Sichuan Regional Command sent troops to repair the bridge at Guanxian as far as Taoguan; the Wenchuan tribal chief Meng Daogui grew suspicious, gathered his tribes, and blocked the road at Taoguan.

value.zh: 都司遣指揮胡淵、童勝等統兵分二道擊之，一由石泉，一由灌口。
value.en: Commanders Hu Yuan and Tong Sheng attacked by Shiquan and Guankou.
value.literal: The Regional Command sent Commanders Hu Yuan and Tong Sheng with troops on two routes to attack—one by Shiquan, one by Guankou.

value.zh: 由灌口者進次陶關，蠻眾伏兩山間，投石崖下，兵不能進。
value.en: The Guankou force reached Taoguan; tribes ambushed from both hills and rolled stones down the cliffs.
value.literal: The Guankou column advanced to Taoguan; the tribes lay in ambush between the two mountains and rolled stones down the cliffs so the army could not advance.

value.zh: 適汶川土官來降，得其間道。
value.en: A Wenchuan chief then surrendered and showed a secret path.
value.literal: Just then a Wenchuan native official came to surrender and revealed a hidden path.

value.zh: 乃選勇士卷旗甲，乘夜潛出兩山後，遲明從山頂張旗幟，發火炮，蠻驚潰。
value.en: Elite troops crept behind the hills by night, raised banners and fired cannon at dawn, and the tribes fled.
value.literal: They therefore chose stalwarts, rolled up banners and armor, stole out by night behind the two mountains, and at dawn unfurled banners from the summits, fired cannon, and the tribes fled in alarm.

value.zh: 師進雁門關，道險，蠻復據之。
value.en: At perilous Yanmen Pass the tribes held the road again.
value.literal: The army advanced to Yanmen Pass; the road was perilous and the tribes again held it.

value.zh: 乃駐平野，得小舟渡，至龍止鐵冶寨，擊破之。
value.en: They crossed by boat, reached Longzhi Tieye Stockade, and stormed it.
value.literal: They camped on the open plain, obtained small boats to cross, reached Longzhi Tieye Stockade, and broke it.

value.zh: 其由石泉者次泥池，蠻悉眾拒。
value.en: The Shiquan column met full tribal resistance at Nichi.
value.literal: The Shiquan column halted at Nichi; the tribes mustered all their strength to resist.

value.zh: 千戶薛文突陣射卻之，士卒奮擊，大敗其眾。
value.en: Commander Xue Wen charged shooting and routed them.
value.literal: Company commander Xue Wen charged the line shooting and drove them back; the soldiers pressed the attack and routed their host.

value.zh: 兩軍遂會於茂州，楊者七迎降，以者七仍領其州。
value.en: Both columns met at Maozhou; Yang Zheqi surrendered and kept his prefecture.
value.literal: The two armies met at Maozhou; Yang Zheqi came out to surrender and Zheqi was left to govern his prefecture.

value.zh: 乃詔立茂州衛，留指揮楚華將兵三千守之。
value.en: Maozhou Guard was founded with Commander Chu Hua and 3,000 troops.
value.literal: An edict then established Maozhou Guard and left Commander Chu Hua with three thousand troops to garrison it.

value.zh: 十五年，者七陰結生番，約日伏兵陷城。
value.en: Year 15: Zheqi secretly allied with raw tribes to ambush the city.
value.literal: In the fifteenth year Zheqi secretly joined the raw tribes and agreed on a day to ambush troops and seize the city.

value.zh: 有小校密告於官，遂發兵捕斬者七。
value.en: A junior officer informed the garrison; Zheqi was captured and beheaded.
value.literal: A junior officer secretly reported to the officials; troops were therefore sent to capture and behead Zheqi.

value.zh: 生番不之覺，如期入寇，官軍掩擊敗之，於是盡徙羌民於城外。
value.en: The raw tribes attacked on schedule and were ambushed; the Qiang were then moved outside the walls.
value.literal: The raw tribes were unaware; they entered on schedule to raid, and government troops ambushed and defeated them, whereupon all Qiang people were moved outside the walls.

value.zh: 呂大防
value.en: Lu Dafang
value.literal: Lu Dafang

value.zh: 頌宴客有美堂，或告將兵欲亂，頌密使捕渠領十輩，荷校付獄中，迨夕會散，坐客不知也。
value.en: While entertaining guests at the Hall of Beauty, Su Song learned that soldiers were plotting a riot; he secretly had ten ringleaders arrested and shackled in prison, and when the banquet ended that evening his guests never knew.
value.literal: Song entertained guests at the Hall of Beauty; someone reported that soldiers were about to riot. Song secretly had ten ringleaders arrested, shackled, and delivered to prison; when evening came the gathering dispersed, and seated guests did not know.

value.zh: 及修兩朝正史，轉右諫議大夫。
value.en: While compiling the standard histories of the two reigns he was promoted to Right Remonstrance Grandee.
value.literal: When the standard histories of the two reigns were compiled, he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Grandee.

value.zh: 使契丹，遇冬至，其國曆後宋曆一日。
value.en: On a mission to the Khitan he encountered the winter solstice; their calendar lagged the Song calendar by one day.
value.literal: On mission to the Khitan, he encountered the winter solstice; their state's calendar lagged the Song calendar by one day.

value.zh: 北人問孰為是，頌曰：「曆家算術小異，遲速不同，如亥時節氣交，猶是今夕；
value.en: The northerners asked which was correct; Su Song said: "Calendar calculations differ slightly in timing. If a solar term arrives in the hour of hai, it is still this evening;
value.literal: Northerners asked which was correct; Song said: "Calendar experts' arithmetic differs slightly; slowness and speed are not the same. If a solar term crosses in the hour of hai, it is still this evening;

value.zh: 若逾數刻，則屬子時，為明日矣。
value.en: but if it passes by several quarters, it falls in the hour of zi and belongs to the next day.
value.literal: if it passes several quarters, then it belongs to the hour of zi and is tomorrow.

value.zh: 或先或後，各從其歷可也。」
value.en: Whether one calendar is ahead or behind, each side may follow its own—that is sufficient."
value.literal: Whether earlier or later, each may follow his own calendar—that will do."

value.zh: 北人以為然。
value.en: The northerners accepted his explanation.
value.literal: The northerners took this as right.

value.zh: 使還以奏，神宗嘉曰：「朕嘗思之，此最難處，卿所對殊善。」
value.en: On his return he reported to the throne; Emperor Shenzong praised him, saying: "I have often pondered this—it is the hardest point to handle, and your answer was excellent."
value.literal: Returning from his mission he memorialized; Emperor Shenzong commended him, saying: "I have pondered this—it is the hardest point to handle; your reply was especially good."

value.zh: 因問其山川、人情向背，對曰：「彼講和日久，頗竊中國典章禮義，以維持其政，上下相安，未有離貳之意。
value.en: He then asked about their terrain and the people's loyalties. Su Song replied: "They have been at peace with us for a long time and have largely adopted Chinese institutions and ritual to sustain their rule; high and low are content, and there is no sign of disaffection.
value.literal: He then asked about their mountains and rivers and the people's inclinations. He replied: "They have been at peace through treaty for a long time and have largely appropriated China's statutes, ritual, and righteousness to sustain their government; above and below are at ease, and there is no intent of division or defection.

value.zh: 昔漢武帝自謂：『高皇帝遺朕平城之憂，雖久勤征討，而匈奴終不服。』
value.en: Emperor Wu of Han once said: 'The High Emperor left me the shame of Pingcheng; though I campaigned for years, the Xiongnu never submitted.'
value.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han said of himself: 'The High Emperor left me the worry of Pingcheng; though I long labored in campaigns and attacks, the Xiongnu in the end did not submit.'

value.zh: 至宣帝，呼韓單于稽首稱藩。
value.en: Yet by Emperor Xuan's reign Chanyu Huhanye bowed his head and declared himself a vassal.
value.literal: By Emperor Xuan's time, Chanyu Huhanye bowed his head and called himself a vassal state.

value.zh: 唐自中葉以後，河湟陷於吐蕃，憲宗每讀《貞觀政要》，慨然有收復意。
value.en: From mid-Tang onward the Hehuang region fell to Tibet; whenever Emperor Xianzong read the 《Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Era》 he sighed with longing to recover it.
value.literal: Tang from the mid-dynasty onward, the Hehuang region fell to the Tibetans; Emperor Xianzong whenever he read the 《Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Era》 would sigh with intent to recover it.

value.zh: 至宣宗時，乃以三關、七州歸於有司。
value.en: By Emperor Xuanzong's reign the Three Passes and Seven Prefectures were restored to imperial control.
value.literal: By Emperor Xuanzong's time, the Three Passes and Seven Prefectures were returned to the regular administration.

value.zh: 由此觀之，外國之叛服不常，不繫中國之盛衰也。」
value.en: From this one sees that foreign peoples submit or rebel regardless of whether China is strong or weak."
value.literal: Viewed from this, foreign states' rebellion and submission are not constant—they are not tied to China's flourishing and decline."

value.zh: 頌意蓋有所諷，神宗然之。
value.en: Su Song's meaning was plainly admonitory, and Emperor Shenzong agreed.
value.literal: Song's meaning probably carried indirect admonition; Emperor Shenzong approved of it.

value.zh: 起昭陽太淵獻，盡玄黓涒灘，凡十年。
value.en: From Zhaoyang Taiyuanxian through Xuanqi Tunshan—ten years in all.
value.literal: From Zhaoyang Taiyuanxian through Xuanqi Tunshan; ten years in all.

value.zh: :班固贊曰：古之制名，必由象類，遠取諸物，近取諸身。
value.en: Ban Gu writes in praise: In antiquity names were fashioned from images and categories—drawing from distant things and from the body itself.
value.literal: Ban Gu's praise says: In antiquity naming was made necessarily from images and categories—taking from distant things, taking from the near body.

value.zh: 故《經》謂君為元首，臣為股肱，明其一體，相待而成也。
value.en: Therefore the Classic calls the ruler the head and limbs and ministers the thighs and arms—making clear they are one body that rely on each other to be whole.
value.literal: Therefore the Classic calls the ruler the head and limbs, ministers the thighs and arms—making clear they are one body, mutually relying to be completed.

value.zh: 是故君臣相配，古今常道，自然之勢也。
value.en: Therefore ruler and ministers match each other—the constant way of past and present and the natural order.
value.literal: Therefore ruler and ministers match each other—the constant way of past and present, the natural tendency.

value.zh: 近觀漢相，高祖開基，蕭、曹為冠；
value.en: Observing Han chancellors at hand: Gaozu laid the foundation, and Xiao and Cao were foremost;
value.literal: Observing Han chancellors near at hand: Gaozu opened the foundation, Xiao and Cao were foremost;

value.zh: 孝宣中興，丙、魏有聲。
value.en: In Emperor Xuan's restoration, Bing and Wei won renown.
value.literal: Emperor Xiao's restoration, Bing and Wei had renown.

value.zh: 是時黜陟有序，眾職修理，公卿多稱其位，海內興於禮讓。
value.en: At that time promotion and demotion were orderly, offices well maintained, ministers and grandees mostly filled their posts, and courtesy and yielding flourished throughout the realm.
value.literal: At that time promotion and demotion were orderly, the multitude of offices well maintained, ministers and grandees mostly filled their posts, and within the seas courtesy and yielding flourished.

value.zh: 覽其行事，豈虛虖哉！
value.en: Review their conduct—was it empty indeed!
value.literal: Reviewing their conduct—was it empty indeed!

value.zh: 二月，壬辰，黃霸為丞相。
value.en: In the second month, on day renchen, Huang Ba became chancellor.
value.literal: Second month, day renchen: Huang Ba became chancellor.

value.zh: 霸材長於治民，及為丞相，功名損於治郡。
value.en: Ba excelled at governing the people; as chancellor his fame and achievement fell short of his record as commandery governor.
value.literal: Ba's talent lay in governing the people; when he became chancellor, his fame and achievement fell short of governing a commandery.

value.zh: 時京兆尹張敞捨鶡雀飛集丞相府，霸以為神雀，議欲以聞。
value.en: At that time Metropolitan Governor Zhang Chang had a magpie from his lodging fly to the chancellor's residence; Ba took it for a divine bird and considered reporting it.
value.literal: At that time Metropolitan Governor Zhang Chang's lodging had a magpie fly and gather at the chancellor's residence; Ba took it for a divine bird and deliberated wishing to report it.

value.zh: 敞奏霸曰：「竊見丞相請與中二千石、博士雜問郡、國上計長史、守丞為民興利除害，成大化，條其對。
value.en: Chang memorialized to Ba, "Your servant has seen the chancellor request to join ranked officials at two thousand shi and academicians in questioning the commandery and state annual-report chief clerks and administrators on benefiting the people and removing harm, accomplishing great transformation, and itemizing their replies.
value.literal: Chang memorialized to Ba, saying: "Your servant has seen the chancellor request to join with ranked officials at two thousand shi and academicians in mixed questioning of the commandery and state annual-report chief clerks and administrators on benefiting the people and removing harm, accomplishing great transformation, and itemizing their replies.

value.zh: 有耕者讓畔，男女異路，道不拾遺。
value.en: There were farmers yielding field boundaries, men and women on separate roads, and no picking up lost things on the road.
value.literal: There were farmers yielding field boundaries, men and women on separate roads, and no picking up lost things on the road.

value.zh: 及舉孝子、貞婦者為一輩，先上殿；
value.en: Those who presented filial sons and chaste wives formed one class and entered the hall first;
value.literal: Those who presented filial sons and chaste wives formed one class and entered the hall first;

value.zh: 舉而不知其人數者，次之；
value.en: those who presented them without knowing the persons' names came next;
value.literal: those who presented them without knowing the persons' names came next;

value.zh: 不為條教者在後。
value.en: those who did not make regulations and teachings came last.
value.literal: those who did not make regulations and teachings came last.

value.zh: 叩頭謝丞相，雖口不言，而心欲其為之也。
value.en: They kowtowed and thanked the chancellor; though they did not speak aloud, they wished in their hearts to do it.
value.literal: They kowtowed and thanked the chancellor; though the mouth did not speak, the heart wished them to do it.

value.zh: 長史、守丞對時，臣敞舍有鶡雀飛止丞相府屋上，丞相以下見者數百人。
value.en: When the chief clerks and administrators replied, a magpie from your servant Chang's lodging flew and perched on the chancellor's roof; from the chancellor down, several hundred people saw it.
value.literal: When the chief clerks and administrators replied, your servant Chang's lodging had a magpie fly and perch on the chancellor's residence roof; from the chancellor down, those who saw it numbered several hundred.

value.zh: 邊吏多知鶡雀者，問之，皆陽不知。
value.en: Many frontier officials knew magpies; when asked, all pretended ignorance.
value.literal: Many frontier officials knew magpies; when asked, all pretended not to know.

value.zh: 丞相圖議上奏曰：『臣問上計長史、守丞以興化條，皇天報下神爵。』
value.en: The chancellor drafted a memorial saying, 'Your servant questioned the annual-report chief clerks and administrators on items for promoting transformation—August Heaven responded by sending down the divine bird.'
value.literal: The chancellor drafted deliberation to memorialize upward, saying: 'Your servant questioned the annual-report chief clerks and administrators on items for promoting transformation—August Heaven responded by sending down the divine bird.'

value.zh: 後知從臣敞舍來，乃止。
value.en: Learning later it came from your servant Chang's lodging, he stopped.
value.literal: Later learning it came from your servant Chang's lodging, he stopped.

value.zh: 郡國吏竊笑丞相仁厚有知略，微信奇怪也。
value.en: Commandery and state officials privately laughed that the chancellor, though benevolent and wise, still slightly believed in the strange.
value.literal: Commandery and state officials privately laughed that the chancellor, though benevolent and thick and possessed of knowledge and strategy, still slightly believed in the strange.

value.zh: 臣敞非敢毀丞相也，誠恐群臣莫白，而長史、守丞畏丞相指，歸捨法令，各為私教，務相增加，澆淳散樸，並行偽貌，有名亡實，傾搖解怠，甚者為妖。
value.en: Your servant Chang does not dare slander the chancellor—he truly fears the ministers will not speak plainly, while chief clerks and administrators, fearing the chancellor's intent, set aside laws and ordinances, each making private teachings and striving to outdo one another, watering down purity and scattering simplicity, all practicing false appearances with name but no substance, growing lax and negligent, and in extreme cases becoming demonic.
value.literal: Your servant Chang does not dare destroy the chancellor—he truly fears the ministers will not speak plainly, while chief clerks and administrators, fearing the chancellor's intent, return and set aside laws and ordinances, each making private teachings, striving to outdo one another, watering down purity and scattering simplicity, all practicing false appearances, having name without substance, leaning and wavering in slackness, and in extreme cases becoming demonic.

value.zh: 假令京師先行讓畔、異路、道不拾遺，其實亡益廉貪、貞淫之行，而以偽先天下，固未可也。
value.en: Suppose the capital region first practiced yielding boundaries, separate roads, and not picking up lost things—in truth it would not improve honest or greedy conduct or chaste or licentious behavior, yet with falsity leading the empire, that truly could not be approved.
value.literal: Suppose the capital region first practiced yielding boundaries, separate roads, and not picking up lost things on the road—in truth it would not benefit honest and greedy conduct or chaste and licentious behavior, yet with falsity leading all under Heaven, it truly could not be approved.

value.zh: 即諸侯先行之，偽聲軼於京師，非細事也。
value.en: If the feudal lords practiced it first, false reputation would outrun the capital—not a small matter.
value.literal: If the feudal lords practiced it first, false reputation would outrun the capital region—not a small matter.

value.zh: 漢家承敝通變，造起律令，所以勸善禁奸，條貫詳備，不可復加。
value.en: The House of Han inherited decline and adapted through change, creating laws and ordinances to encourage good and forbid wickedness—provisions thorough and complete, not to be added to again.
value.literal: The House of Han inherited decline and adapted through change, creating laws and ordinances to encourage good and forbid wickedness—articles thorough and complete, not to be added to again.

value.zh: 宜令貴臣明飭長史、守丞，歸告二千石，舉三老、孝弟、力田、孝廉、廉吏，務得其人，郡事皆以法令為檢式，毋得擅為條教；
value.en: Noble ministers ought clearly to instruct chief clerks and administrators to tell the two-thousand-shi officials to present the three elders, filial and brotherly men, strength-in-farming men, filial and incorrupt candidates, and honest officials, striving to obtain the right men; commandery affairs should all take laws and ordinances as the standard, and none may on their own authority make regulations and teachings;
value.literal: One ought to order noble ministers clearly to instruct chief clerks and administrators, return and tell the two-thousand-shi officials, present the three elders, filial and brotherly, strength-in-farming, filial and incorrupt, and honest officials, striving to obtain the right men; commandery affairs should all take laws and ordinances as models and measures, and none may on their own authority make regulations and teachings;

value.zh: 敢挾詐偽以干名譽者，必先受戮，以正明好惡。」
value.en: whoever dares to rely on fraud and falsity to seek fame and reputation should first be punished, to rectify likes and dislikes."
value.literal: whoever dares to rely on fraud and falsity to seek fame and reputation should first receive punishment, to rectify and clarify likes and dislikes."

value.zh: 天子嘉納敞言，召上計吏，使侍中臨飭，如敞指意。
value.en: The emperor praised and accepted Chang's words, summoned the annual-report clerks, and had a palace attendant oversee and instruct them according to Chang's intent.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven praised and accepted Chang's words, summoned the annual-report clerks, and had a palace attendant oversee and instruct them according to Chang's intent.

value.zh: 霸甚慚。
value.en: Ba was deeply ashamed.
value.literal: Ba was deeply ashamed.

value.zh: :臣光曰：以孝宣之明，魏相、丙吉為丞相，于定國為廷尉，而趙、蓋、韓、楊之死皆不厭眾心，惜哉，其為善政之累大矣！
value.en: Your servant Guang says: With Emperor Xuan's clarity, Wei Xiang and Bing Ji as chancellors, and Yu Dingguo as Minister of Justice, yet the deaths of Zhao, Gai, Han, and Yang all failed to satisfy popular sentiment-alas, how great the burden on good government!
value.literal: Your servant Guang says: With Emperor Xiao Xuan's clarity, Wei Xiang and Bing Ji as chancellors, and Yu Dingguo as Minister of Justice, yet the deaths of Zhao, Gai, Han, and Yang all failed to satisfy the people's hearts-alas, how great the burden on good government!

value.zh: 《周官》司寇之法，有議賢、議能。
value.en: In the Zhou Offices, the Minister of Crime's law provides deliberation for the worthy and deliberation for the capable.
value.literal: In the Zhou Offices, the Minister of Crime's law has deliberation for the worthy and deliberation for the capable.

value.zh: 若廣漢、延壽之治民，可不謂能乎！
value.en: If Guanghan and Yanshou's governing of the people—can they not be called capable!
value.literal: If Guanghan and Yanshou's governing of the people—can they not be called capable!

value.zh: 寬饒、惲之剛直，可不謂賢乎！
value.en: Kuanrao and Yun's firm uprightness—can they not be called worthy!
value.literal: Kuanrao and Yun's firm uprightness—can they not be called worthy!

value.zh: 然則雖有死罪，猶將宥之，況罪不足以死乎！
value.en: If so, though there were a death offense, one would still pardon them—how much more when the offense did not warrant death!
value.literal: If so, though there were a death offense, one would still pardon them—how much more when the offense was not enough to die!

value.zh: 揚子以韓馮翊之愬蕭為臣之自失。
value.en: Master Yang held that Governor of Han, Fengyi's suing Xiao was a minister losing himself.
value.literal: Master Yang held that Governor of Han, Fengyi's suing Xiao was a minister's losing himself.

value.zh: 夫所以使延壽犯上者，望之激之也。
value.en: What made Yanshou offend his superior was Wang Zhi provoking him.
value.literal: What made Yanshou offend his superior was Wang Zhi's provoking him.

value.zh: 上不之察，而延壽獨蒙其辜，不亦甚哉！
value.en: The emperor did not examine it, yet Yanshou alone bore the guilt—is it not extreme!
value.literal: The emperor did not examine it, yet Yanshou alone bore the guilt—is it not extreme!

value.zh: 匈奴閏振單于率其眾東擊郅支單于。
value.en: Chanyu Runzhen of the Xiongnu led his forces east to attack Chanyu Zhizhi.
value.literal: Chanyu Runzhen of the Xiongnu led his masses east to attack Chanyu Zhizhi.

value.zh: 郅支與戰，殺之，併其兵；
value.en: Zhizhi fought him, killed him, and absorbed his troops;
value.literal: Zhizhi fought with him, killed him, and merged his troops;

value.zh: 遂進攻呼韓邪。
value.en: then he advanced to attack Huhanye.
value.literal: thereupon he advanced to attack Huhanye.

value.zh: 呼韓邪兵敗走，郅支都單于庭。
value.en: Huhanye was defeated and fled; Zhizhi occupied the Chanyu's court.
value.literal: Huhanye's army was defeated and fled; Zhizhi occupied the Chanyu's court.

value.zh: :臣光曰：王霸無異道。
value.en: Minister Guang said: The ways of king and hegemon are not different paths.
value.literal: Minister Guang said: The ways of king and hegemon are not different paths.

value.zh: 昔三代之隆，禮樂、征伐自天子出，則謂之王。
value.en: In antiquity at the height of the Three Dynasties, when rites, music, and campaigns issued from the Son of Heaven, it was called kingship.
value.literal: In antiquity at the height of the Three Dynasties, when rites and music and campaigns and punishments issued from the Son of Heaven, it was called kingship.

value.zh: 天子微弱不能治諸侯，諸侯有能率其與國同討不庭以尊王室者，則謂之霸。
value.en: When the Son of Heaven was weak and could not govern the feudal lords, and a lord was able to lead allied states to punish the disobedient and honor the royal house, it was called hegemony.
value.literal: When the Son of Heaven was weak and could not govern the feudal lords, and a feudal lord was able to lead the states allied with him jointly to punish the disobedient and honor the royal house, it was called hegemony.

value.zh: 其所以行之也，皆本仁祖義，任賢使能，賞善罰惡，禁暴誅亂。
value.en: The means by which both were carried out all took benevolence as root and righteousness as model, employed the worthy, rewarded good and punished evil, and forbade violence.
value.literal: The means by which they were carried out all took benevolence as root and righteousness as model, employed the worthy and used the able, rewarded good and punished evil, forbade violence and executed disorder.

value.zh: 顧名位有尊卑，德澤有深淺，功業有鉅細，政令有廣狹耳，非若白黑、甘苦之相反也。
value.en: Only that rank had high and low, favor had depth, achievements had scale, and orders had scope—that is all; it is not like black and white or sweet and bitter in opposition.
value.literal: Only that name and position had high and low, virtue's favor had deep and shallow, achievements had large and small, and government orders had broad and narrow—that is all; it is not like black and white or sweet and bitter in mutual opposition.

value.zh: 漢之所以不能復三代之治者，由人主之不為，非先王之道不可復行於後世也。
value.en: The reason Han could not restore Three Dynasties governance was that rulers did not do it—not that the former kings' Way could not be practiced again.
value.literal: The reason Han could not restore the governance of the Three Dynasties was that the human ruler did not do it—not that the former kings' Way could not again be practiced in later generations.

value.zh: 夫儒有君子，有小人。
value.en: Among Confucians there are gentlemen and petty men.
value.literal: Among Confucians there are gentlemen and there are petty men.

value.zh: 彼俗儒者，誠不足與為治也，獨不可求真儒而用之乎？
value.en: Those vulgar Confucians truly are not fit to govern with—but cannot one seek true Confucians and employ them?
value.literal: Those vulgar Confucians truly are not fit to govern with—but can one alone not seek true Confucians and employ them?

value.zh: 稷、契、皋陶、伯益、伊尹、周公、孔子，皆大儒也，使漢得而用之，功烈豈若是而止邪！
value.en: Ji, Qi, Gao Yao, Bo Yi, Yi Yin, Duke of Zhou, and Confucius were all great Confucians; had Han obtained and employed them, would achievements have stopped at this!
value.literal: Ji, Qi, Gao Yao, Bo Yi, Yi Yin, Duke of Zhou, and Confucius were all great Confucians; had Han obtained and employed them, would achievements and glory have stopped like this!

value.zh: 孝宣謂太子懦而不立，闇於治體，必亂我家，則可矣；
value.en: Emperor Xuan's saying the heir apparent was weak, unfit to stand, ignorant of governance, and would disorder his house—that could pass;
value.literal: Emperor Xuan's saying the heir apparent was weak and could not stand, dark to the body of governance, and would surely disorder his house—that could pass;

value.zh: 乃曰王道不可行，儒者不可用，豈不過甚矣哉！
value.en: yet to say the kingly Way could not be practiced and Confucians could not be employed—was that not going too far!
value.literal: yet to say the kingly Way could not be practiced and Confucians could not be employed—was that not going too far!

value.zh: 殆非所以訓示子孫，垂法將來者也。
value.en: It was hardly the way to instruct posterity or hand down law for the future.
value.literal: It was nearly not the means to instruct and show sons and grandsons or to hand down law for the future.

value.zh: 淮陽憲王好法律，聰達有材；
value.en: Prince Xian of Huaiyang was fond of law, clever and talented;
value.literal: Prince Xian of Huaiyang was fond of law, clever and penetrating with talent;

value.zh: 王母張婕妤尤幸。
value.en: his queen mother, Lady Zhang the Beautiful Companion, was especially favored.
value.literal: his queen mother, Lady Zhang the Beautiful Companion, was especially favored.

value.zh: 上由是疏太子而愛淮陽憲王，數嗟歎憲王曰：「真我子也！」
value.en: The emperor thereby grew distant from the heir apparent and loved Prince Xian of Huaiyang, repeatedly sighing and saying, "Truly my son!"
value.literal: The emperor thereby grew distant from the heir apparent and loved Prince Xian of Huaiyang, repeatedly sighing in admiration of the prince and saying: "Truly my son!"

value.zh: 常有意欲立憲王，然用太子起於微細，上少依倚許氏，及即位而許后以殺死，故弗忍也。
value.en: He constantly intended to establish Prince Xian, yet because the heir apparent had risen from humble origins, the emperor in youth had relied on the Xu clan, and after accession Empress Xu died by execution, he could not bear to do it.
value.literal: He constantly had intent to establish Prince Xian, yet because the heir apparent had risen from minute origins and the emperor in youth had relied on the Xu clan, and after accession the Empress Xu died by killing, he therefore could not bear it.

value.zh: 久之，上拜韋玄成為淮陽中尉，以玄成嘗讓爵于兄，欲以感諭憲王。
value.en: After a long time, the emperor appointed Wei Xuancheng Commandant of Huaiyang, because Xuancheng had once yielded his noble rank to his elder brother, wishing thereby to instruct Prince Xian by example.
value.literal: After a long time, the emperor appointed Wei Xuancheng as Commandant of Huaiyang, because Xuancheng had once yielded his noble rank to his elder brother, wishing thereby to move and instruct Prince Xian.

value.zh: 由是太子遂安。
value.en: Thereby the heir apparent was at last secure.
value.literal: Thereby the heir apparent was at last secure.

value.zh: 匈奴呼韓邪單于之敗也，左伊秩訾王為呼韓邪計，勸令稱臣入朝事漢，從漢求助，如此，匈奴乃定。
value.en: When Chanyu Huhanye of the Xiongnu was defeated, the Left Yizhi Zhi King advised him to declare himself a subject, attend court, and serve Han, seeking Han's aid—thus the Xiongnu would be settled.
value.literal: When the Xiongnu Chanyu Huhanye was defeated, the Left Yizhi Zhi King made a plan for Huhanye, urging him to declare himself a subject, enter court, and serve Han, follow Han to seek aid—thus the Xiongnu would be settled.

value.zh: 呼韓邪問諸大臣，皆曰：「不可。
value.en: Huhanye asked the great ministers; all said, "It cannot be done.
value.literal: Huhanye asked the various great ministers; all said: "It cannot be done.

value.zh: 匈奴之俗，本上氣力而下服役，以馬上戰鬥為國，故有威名於百蠻。
value.en: Xiongnu custom esteems strength above and servitude below; taking battle on horseback as the foundation of state, they have prestige among the hundred barbarians.
value.literal: The Xiongnu custom esteems above physical strength and below servitude; taking battle on horseback as the state, therefore they have a prestigious name among the hundred barbarians.

value.zh: 戰死，壯士所有也。
value.en: To die in battle is a stalwart man's portion.
value.literal: To die in battle is what a stalwart man possesses.

value.zh: 今兄弟爭國，不在兄則在弟，雖死猶有威名，子孫常長諸國。
